title: Concept Card Workshop
user: Instructors teaching procedural or safety concepts who need a fast way to run a small-group, discussion-led card exercise after a lecture.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A learner describes a difficult avalanche-risk lecture becoming understandable when the instructor switched to physical Snow Safety Cards, and asks about games/cards for learning skills.
A parent reports that a daughter who uses flashcards heavily encountered a serious scheduling-algorithm failure, reinforcing the value of activities that do not depend on a black-box review queue.

recurrence: The 2026 firsthand classroom-to-cards account and 2025 heavy-user reliability issue both favor transparent, instructor-led practice over a fragile individual SRS loop.
current_workaround: Buy specialized card decks, improvise slips of paper, or lecture again with discussion questions.
incumbents_and_gap: Quizlet Live and Kahoot are screen-centric competition products; commercial training decks are domain-specific. Teachers lack a neutral printable builder for scenario, evidence, decision, and consequence cards.
smallest_useful_product: A static-web card-set composer with four card roles, printable cut sheets, a facilitator timer, and a no-account join code for optional projection. Non-goals: graded assessments, public marketplaces, generated lesson content, or student profiling.
success_measure: Ten pilot facilitators each run one 15-minute activity; at least 70% report every group contributed one defensible decision in the debrief.
monetization: freemium — free single-set printing invites teacher adoption; paid offline pack templates can support niche professional training.
constraints: No bundled regulated/safety curriculum; teacher owns content and outcomes; printable PDFs need accessible text alternatives and browser-only generation.
why_distinct: It creates facilitated reasoning games from teacher-authored material, not another solitary flashcard or points quiz.
